question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{{x}^{6}}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{{x}^{6}}{3})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{{x}^{6}}{3})}^{2}}\cdot {(\frac{{x}^{6}}{3})}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{(1-\frac{{x}^{12}}{9})}\cdot 2{x}^{5} \\  & =\frac{9{x}^{5}}{9-{x}^{12}}.\end{aligned}
$$
